extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry (JASMS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting manuscripts (Articles, Communications, Technical Notes, Reviews, Tutorials, Perspectives, Accounts, Letters) to the Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry, including formatting, scope, ethical and editorial policies, and production requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers all aspects of mass spectrometry, including applications and fundamentals across chemical, biological, health, environmental, forensic sciences, omics sciences (proteomics, metabolomics), physics, and geology; includes instrumentation and methods development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers reporting applications should focus principally on use of a new mass spectrometry tool or approach to solve a qualitative or quantitative problem. Routine applications are better suited to specialized journals. Computer applications, algorithms, and software will be considered but extensive program compilations/details will not be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate manuscript type
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal accepts Articles, Communications, Technical Notes, Letters, Methods/Protocols, Perspectives, Tutorials, Reviews, and Accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each type has distinct aims and expectations (e.g., Perspectives summarize a body of research; Tutorials teach how to accomplish a specific application). Some (Perspectives, Reviews, Accounts) are typically invited but proposals may be submitted to the Editor-in-Chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Communications and Technical Notes limits and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Short Communications: brief descriptions of new and significant research, often establishing priority; Technical Notes: brief descriptions of technical advances in sample handling, instrumentation, data processing, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both may contain up to three single-column figures or tables (up to one page total) and up to 2,300 words (including references and abstract). Space for figures/tables may be replaced by text (~250 words per figure/table). Submissions exceeding guidelines will be treated as Regular Articles. They receive expedited handling when possible. Communications must contain some experimental or theoretical justification for the ideas being presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the Editor policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters should be brief and may be edited for conciseness and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters commenting on research previously published in this journal will be forwarded to original author for possible rebuttal; the journal will not accept Letters to the Editor that comment on research published elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications/Technical Notes figure/text tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Space allocated to figures and tables may be replaced by text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate ~250 words per figure or table when replacing figures with text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Fast Format for initial submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All ACS journals have a streamlined standardized format for initial manuscript submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial submissions must be complete with clearly identified standard sections, free of annotations or highlights, and include all numbered and labeled components. Figures, charts, tables, schemes, and equations should be embedded in the text at the point of relevance. Separate graphics can be supplied later at revision if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript templates when required
rubrics_metrics.description: When required by a journal's structure or length limitations, manuscript templates should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates facilitate peer review by allowing artwork and tables close to the discussion point. Refer to ACS templates and the ACS Guide to Scholarly Communication for general preparation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: References formatting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: References can be provided in any style but must be complete, including titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Chemical Abstracts Service Source Index abbreviations for journal names. Number references consecutively in the order mentioned. Provide full citation elements: authors' names, article title, year, volume, and page numbers (inclusive pagination recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter must accompany every manuscript submission and may be typed/pasted into the submission system or attached as a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: full manuscript title; corresponding author name and complete contact info (mailing address, phone, email); names of other authors; statement of why paper is appropriate for JASMS; description of Supporting Information for Publication and/or Review Only; four or more suggested reviewers with contact information; link to preprint if deposited and statement of how manuscript was updated since preprint; any related/prior work to disclose. Note any length issues and prior discussion with an Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise paper title and a running title of no more than 45 characters (including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List 'Address reprint requests to...' with name, exact postal address, telephone, and e-mail of corresponding author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract no longer than 250 words for an Article, Short Communication, Note, and Perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An abstract is not required for a Letter to the Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main body organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize text as Introduction, Experimental or Methods, Theory (if applicable), Results and Discussion, and Conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions should not be a repetition of the abstract or a summary of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental section safety reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all special safety considerations in sufficient detail in the Experimental section so appropriate safety measures can be taken by those repeating the experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Communications or Letters, include safety information in the main text. Statement examples are provided in the Safety Statement Style Sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out or define in parentheses all abbreviations at first use in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-standard abbreviations should be used sparingly and must be defined at first appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomenclature and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use IUPAC-recommended nomenclature for chemical compounds; for mass spectrometry nomenclature follow IUPAC rules and Standard Definitions of Terms Relating to Mass Spectrometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult referenced sources (Todd 1991; Price; Sparkman Mass Spec Desk Reference) for additional suggestions on definitions and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and mass units
rubrics_metrics.description: Give all measurements and weights in SI units using standard abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daltons (Da) or mass units (u) may be used; amu should not be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations, chemical structures, and schemes numbering/formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Number equations consecutively with Arabic numerals (right-hand side). Number chemical structures consecutively with boldface Arabic numerals. Designate schemes showing fragmentation pathways or reactions by consecutive capital Roman numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add spaces before and after mathematical symbols (e.g., +, -, =) to distinguish them from chemical bonds. Schemes usually do not have titles or captions; distinguish pathways within schemes by lower-case letters on arrows if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and illustrations: content and necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer initial submission with figures, tables, and schemes embedded in the main body. All tables should have short, descriptive titles; figures should have captions and be numbered with Arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a figure is essential; avoid figures containing principally 'white space' (e.g., broad-range spectra better described in text or table). Restrict number of figures for a full article to eight and to three for a communication or note (seek permission if more needed). Place keys to symbols preferably within artwork, not only in captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures captions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure must have a caption giving the figure number and a brief description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caption should be understandable without reference to the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: titles and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Each table must have a brief (one phrase or sentence) title that describes the contents and should be understandable without reference to the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put details in footnotes not the title. Use tables when narrative cannot clearly present data or when many numbers are required. Tables should be simple and concise—avoid merging or splitting cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Information submission and descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting Information must be submitted at the same time as the manuscript and is provided to reviewers (Review Only) and, if appropriate, to readers (Publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a brief, nonsentence description of the actual contents of each file including file type extension, labeled 'Supporting Information' before Acknowledgement and References. Examples of sufficient descriptions: 'H NMR spectra for all compounds (PDF)'. Insufficient examples: 'Figures S1-S3'. When including Review Only files, include copies of unpublished or in-press references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Data policy and data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to make the research data underlying their articles publicly available at time of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research data includes primary data, secondary data used/analyzed, and any materials necessary to reproduce results. See ACS Research Data Policy for Data Availability Statements, Data Citation, and recommended repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-resolution mass spectral data for formula confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: When exact-mass data are used to confirm identities, report the uncertainty in the accurate-mass measurement used for formula verification along with the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate uncertainty by any statistically valid method (e.g., precision and accuracy of replicate measurements or instrument performance). Do not set fixed acceptable error limits for exact mass measurement; consider all candidate formulae fitting the experimentally determined value and its reported uncertainty when using accurate mass for formula confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics resolution minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital graphics pasted into manuscripts must meet minimum resolution requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Black and white line art: 1200 dpi; Grayscale art: 600 dpi; Color art: 300 dpi. Graphics must be prepared and submitted in digital format; figures are not modified by production staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics size, fonts, and line weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics must fit one- or two-column formats with specific width and depth limits; lettering should be legible in final published format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-column max width 240 points (3.33 in); double-column 300–504 points (4.167–7 in). Maximum depth including caption 660 points (9.167 in). Allow 12 pts per caption text line. Lettering no smaller than 4.5 points in final format. Use Helvetica or Arial; lines no thinner than 0.5 point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color usage and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Color may be used to enhance clarity but graphics intended to appear in black/white should not be submitted in color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on color alone—use symbols, text labels, or patterns. Ensure sufficient contrast (WCAG guidance: contrast ratio 4.5:1 for text; 3:1 for nontext elements with exceptions). Use suggested color schemes for accessibility and tools (TPGi Contrast Checker, Colour Contrast Analyzer). If color is necessary, choose accurate and accessible combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable software and file designations; submission platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit manuscripts, graphics, supporting information, and required forms through ACS Publishing Center; ACS ID required to log in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript File as single .doc or .docx with figures, tables, and captions. Supporting Information as separate file(s). A Manuscript PDF is optional and, if uploaded, will be used for the peer-review PDF proof. Authors must view and approve PDF proof prior to formal submission. Consult list of acceptable software and compatible file types in submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required files at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must submit separate files: Manuscript file (.doc/.docx), cover letter, Supporting Information for Publication (if applicable), and any additional materials for review (as Supporting Information for Review Only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Manuscript PDF file is optional. If a PDF is uploaded, it may be used as the PDF proof during peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication and preprint policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal considers original work not previously published and not under consideration elsewhere; related work under consideration must be cited and disclosed at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are allowed to deposit initial draft on recognized preprint servers (ChemRxiv, bioRxiv, arXiv) prior to submission. Note preprint use in cover letter and include link and description of updates made. Upon publication, authors are advised to add link from preprint to published paper via DOI. Electronic posting of conference presentations or posters behind subscription/institutional logins are not considered prior publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship consent and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to obtain consent of all coauthors prior to submitting a manuscript. The submitting author must notify all coauthors that the manuscript is being submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contact information for all coauthors during submission (full name, email, institutional affiliation, mailing address). Author affiliation should reflect where the work was completed; include current addresses as a note if applicable. Any changes to authorship after initial submission require an authorship change form and confirmation that all authors agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship change and justification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to authorship after submission require completion of an authorship change form and confirmation that all authors agree to the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a reason for each change and explain how added coauthors meet authorship criteria. Authorship changes are subject to editorial approval; additions post-acceptance generally not considered except in rare, justified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI tools use and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools do not qualify for authorship and must be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of AI tool use for text or image generation should be in the Acknowledgments with a description of when and how tools were used. For substantial use, provide full details in Methods or appropriate section. Authors are responsible for all submitted content and must ensure generated content is appropriate and complies with Ethical Guidelines and ACS AI Best Practices and Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement describing any financial conflicts of interest or lack thereof is published in each article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During submission, the Corresponding Author must provide a statement on behalf of all authors describing potential sources of bias (affiliations, funding, financial/management relationships). If none, the published statement will read: 'The authors declare no competing financial interest.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and similarity screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts may be examined using software to detect duplication of already published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACS Publications uses CrossCheck's iThenticate to screen submitted manuscripts for similarity to published material. See Ethical Guidelines Part B for more on CrossCheck participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial pre-screen (desk rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may identify submissions that in their expert opinion would not fare well during review and reject without external reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often more than one Editor will be consulted during initial screening. Desk rejection shortens time to decision and manages reviewer workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript evaluation criteria for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate manuscripts based on originality, technical quality, clarity of presentation, and importance to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors evaluate reviewers' arguments in the context of the journal's scope and aims to make final decisions (accept; revise; reject but consider resubmission after significant work; decline for major flaws, insufficient advance, or lack of novelty/interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting potential reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should suggest four or more individuals competent to review the manuscript, with contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid suggesting reviewers from real or perceived conflicts of interest (e.g., authors' institutions). Prefer academic email addresses rather than personal addresses where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript revisions deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmit manuscripts for which revisions were requested within one month of receipt of the reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts received after this period may be regarded as new submissions and may be subject to re-review to ensure currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals are reviewed at editorial discretion and should be initiated by the corresponding author via formal appeal letter within one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal letter should include: manuscript ID; a clear rationale for disagreement; point-by-point responses to reviewer/editor comments; evidence of errors, potential reviewer conflicts of interest, or other ethical considerations. Only one appeal per manuscript; appeals are considered an extension of submission process and same ethical guidelines apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer between ACS journals
rubrics_metrics.description: If declined, editors may suggest transfer to another ACS or partner journal; transfer copies coauthors, suggested reviewers, manuscript files, and responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transferring simplifies submitting to a different ACS journal but does not guarantee acceptance; the receiving journal's editor makes final decision. Authors are free to accept or decline transfer offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs and Corresponding Author responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of galley proofs is the responsibility of the Corresponding Author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding Author will receive notification when page proofs are available via ACS Direct Correct and should return proofs within 48 hours to ensure timely publication. Extensive or important changes on page proofs (including title or list of authors) are subject to editor review. Corresponding Author must ensure all authors agree with changes made on proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date and patent considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted manuscripts will be published on ACS Publications website as soon as page proofs are corrected and author concerns resolved; the first web publication date is the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication may occur weeks before cover date—authors should resolve patent/IP matters prior to first publication (ASAP or issue) and ensure patent information is available at time of first publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASAP publication and DOI assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are published ASAP after proofs corrections; all articles published ahead of print receive a DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental information receives a DOI and will be hosted on Figshare to promote open data discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication corrections, expressions of concern, and retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Additions and Corrections may be requested by authors or initiated by the Editor to correct errors of consequence; retractions and expressions of concern follow COPE guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions/Corrections must be submitted as new manuscripts by Corresponding Author with approval from coauthors. Articles may be retracted for scientific or ethical reasons; a Retraction notice will explain the reason and the original article will normally remain online except in extraordinary circumstances. Expressions of Concern may be issued when evidence is inconclusive or investigations are unfair/incomplete; these may be replaced by Retractions or Corrections after investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OFAC and compliance with U.S. sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: As a U.S.-based organization, ACS must comply with U.S. sanctions laws administered by OFAC and may be prohibited from publishing activities with certain authors or institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACS reserves the right to refrain from publishing activities that it determines may violate U.S. law, including cases involving Specially Designated Nationals (SDNs).

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement for revisions and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submitting manuscript revisions are required to provide a validated personal ORCID iD before completing submission (if not already associated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCID may be provided during original submission or when submitting a revision. ORCID iDs should not be typed into the manuscript. ACS publishes only verified ORCID iDs associated with ACS before manuscript acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funder reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to report funding sources and grant/award numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter funding sources using the Funder Registry Tool in the submission system and in your manuscript to meet reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion and citation statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may optionally submit an inclusion statement relevant to their paper, and ACS recommends a citation statement in Acknowledgements addressing inclusive citation practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion statements may include analysis of citations and acknowledgement of indigenous land. Political beliefs are not permitted. Citation statement should include: (1) importance of inclusive citation practices, (2) proportion of citations by gender and race/ethnicity for first and last authors, (3) method used and limitations, (4) steps to mitigate citation bias. Land acknowledgments should link to formal institutional land acknowledgments where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover art and supplementary covers
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal selects papers for cover artwork; authors may suggest cover ideas and submit artwork/caption when submitting a manuscript revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any use of AI in cover art must comply with ACS AI Best Practices and be disclosed in the cover caption. Contact ACSPubsMultimedia@acs.org for questions about AI use in cover art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web Enhanced Objects (WEO) submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Web editions allow multimedia attachments (animations, movies) as Web Enhanced Objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload WEOs in the submission system with 'Web Enhanced Object' file designation and consult the list of compatible WEO formats.
